claims.quote: a child experiencing epilepsy with myoclonic-atonic seizures (EMAS) attributed to a variant in the SLC6A1 gene.

claims.object_text: delays in intellectual and language development
claims.quote: The male child showed delays in intellectual and language development before the disease began.

claims.object_text: generalized tonic-clonic, myoclonic, and myoclonic-atonic seizures
claims.quote: these seizures presented as generalized tonic-clonic, myoclonic, and myoclonic-atonic seizures
At 1 year and 2 months, he had a febrile seizures
along with symptoms showing inattention and hyperactivity.
Genetic analysis indicated a heterozygous missense variant of c.263T > C (p.L88P) in the SLC6A1 gene in the child
After receiving treatment with levetiracetam (50 mg·kg·d-1), the child has been free of seizures for the last 8 months.
The variant in the SLC6A1 gene is implicated as one of the etiological factors contributing to EMAS coupled with neurodevelopmental abnormalities.
